items.title: Steve Angrum Interview, 1961-08-08
items.q: Well, I was going to ask about the Tushaline when he taught, did he have you bite onto the upper part of the mouthpiece of your teeth on? ... Yeah, he always taught you to put the horn in the direct center.

ctx.x: I went off and he used B flat climbing on the parade, but still no, he don't get up there and make the modern note. No. No. Do you think that playing the sax might spoil them a little bit for a crying act? It do. Do you think that? It does, yeah. Mm-hmm. I've sort of noticed that myself. Yeah, I do. It seems like you get a different armature for that big- For that big mouthpiece. Yeah. Yeah. It's for the cranny. Yeah.
Mm-hmm. Well, I was going to ask about the Tushaline when he taught, did he have you bite onto the upper part of the mouthpiece of your teeth on?

Did you ever cover your both lips? Yeah, he always taught you to put the horn in the direct center. You see? Of your mouth. Of your mouth. Yeah, and don't let it touch your bottom teeth. What is it? Don't touch your bottom teeth, but you can touch, you know, the top. Yeah, bite onto the upper teeth. On the upper teeth, yeah. But you don't, do you actually bite on it, or? No, you don't bite on it. You just, you don't have a hole in it, you know? Yeah, it's a hole. You see, like, press fine, like when you're…
